title: Does System-Prompt Persona Diversity Reduce Inter-Model Homogeneity?

original_idea.body:
# Does System-Prompt Persona Diversity Reduce Inter-Model Homogeneity?

**Problem:** A cheap proposed monoculture fix is to give models different personas. Whether persona steering actually decorrelates the underlying answers (vs just changing surface style) on safety-relevant content has not been measured.

**Direction:** Run each of several models under a panel of distinct personas. Decompose homogeneity into stylistic vs substantive similarity. Test whether persona diversity moves substantive answers or only style.

**Why it matters:** If persona steering is cosmetic, operators relying on it for diversity/safety are fooling themselves.

**Relevant context:** RLHF style-mode findings (arXiv:2310.06452); Verbalized Sampling (arXiv:2510.01171); Artificial Hivemind.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible: tests whether persona-based diversity is cosmetic; useful but indirect safety payoff.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Prompt-only, no training, with style-vs-substance decomposition; very accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused with/without-persona comparison; the style/substance split is a modest analysis dependency.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Prompt-only, public models; evaluates a mitigation labs underpublish.

novelty.reasoning: Persona steering studied; style-vs-substance decorrelation on safety partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Persona prompting studied; substantive inter-model decorrelation slice partly open.
